модуль ara::tsync — Time Synchronization

Спецификация: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf (R25-11) · 141 запись API

function: 70 variable: 37 type alias: 12 class: 10 struct: 8 enumeration: 4

Руководство пользователя Сгенерировано ИИ / AI generated

Автоматически создаваемое описание, контент получен из ссылочных документов AUTOSAR R25-11 (спецификация SWS и сопроводительные стандартные документы) — не официальный текст AUTOSAR. Утверждения, помеченные как интерпретация, представляют собой выводы, сделанные на основе источников.

Rolle & Verwendungszweck

Time Synchronization (ara::tsync) stellt der AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform hochpräzise, netzwerkweit synchronisierte Zeitbasen bereit. In modernen Fahrzeugarchitekturen ist eine konsistente Zeitreferenz über mehrere Steuergeräte hinweg unerlässlich — insbesondere für Sensorfusion, bild- und radargestützte Fahrerassistenzsysteme (ADAS), deterministische Ereignisprotokollierung sowie echtzeitkritische Regelungen [SWS_TS_00001].

Das Modul realisiert die Anbindung an standardisierte Zeitsynchronisationsprotokolle wie gPTP (IEEE 802.1AS / IEEE 1588) über Ethernet sowie busspezifische Zeitsynchronisationsmechanismen (z. B. CAN-TSyn). Es unterscheidet funktional zwischen Time Master (Knoten, die als globale Zeitquelle fungieren oder Zeitinformationen weiterverteilen) und Time Slave (Knoten, die externe Zeitbotschaften empfangen, Pfadverzögerungen kompensieren und die lokale Uhr disziplinieren) [SWS_TS_00010].

Architektur- und Schnittstellenverträge

Die C++-Schnittstellen von ara::tsync orientieren sich eng an den Standards von std::chrono und bieten darüber hinaus spezialisierte Verträge für automobilrelevante Zeitstatusprüfungen:

  • SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer: Zentraler API-Einstiegspunkt für Anwendungen, die eine synchronisierte Zeitbasis konsumieren [SWS_TS_01001]. Über GetCurrentTime() wird ein synchronisierter Zeitstempel als ara::core::Result<TimePoint> abgerufen [SWS_TS_01007].
  • Ratenabweichung und Zeitstatus: Mit GetRateDeviation() lässt sich die aktuelle Frequenz- bzw. Ratenabweichung der Uhr (Drift) ermitteln [SWS_TS_01008]. Die Methode GetTimeWithStatus() liefert den Zeitwert atomar zusammen mit dem aktuellen Gültigkeits- und Synchronisationszustand [SWS_TS_01009].
  • Ereignis- und Statussignalisierung: Anwendungen können Callback-Handler für Statuswechsel (RegisterStatusChangeNotifier() [SWS_TS_01010]), Änderungen des Synchronisationszustands (RegisterSynchronizationStateChangeNotifier() [SWS_TS_01012]) sowie Zeitspünge (RegisterTimeLeapNotifier() [SWS_TS_01014]) registrieren. Zur Überwachung der Einhaltung vorgegebener Präzisionskorridore dient RegisterTimePrecisionMeasurementNotifier() [SWS_TS_01018].
  • Statusobjekt SynchronizedTimeBaseStatus: Kapselt Metadaten zum Synchronisationszustand, darunter Erstellungszeitpunkt (GetCreationTime() [SWS_TS_01055]), Synchronisationsstatus (GetSynchronizationStatus() [SWS_TS_01053]), erkannte Zeitsprünge (GetLeapJump() [SWS_TS_01054]) sowie anwendungsspezifische Benutzerdaten (GetUserData() [SWS_TS_01056]).
  • SynchronizedTimeBaseProvider: Dient Subsystemen, die selbst als lokale oder externe Zeitquelle agieren, zur Bereitstellung und periodischen Einspeisung der Zeitbasis samt Zeitvalidierungsnotifikationen [SWS_TS_01114].

Interaktionsfluss

Im laufenden Betrieb synchronisiert der Hintergrunddienst von ara::tsync die lokale Uhr kontinuierlich anhand eingehender Protokollbotschaften (z. B. PTP-Sync- und Follow-Up-Frames). Sobald die Zeitabweichung unter den konfigurierten Schwellwert sinkt, meldet das System den Zustand kSynchronized über registrierte Notifier. Konsumierende Anwendungen können jederzeit hochpräzise Zeitstempel abfragen oder auf Statusänderungen reagieren.

Interaktionsdiagramm: Zeitsynchronisation und Abfrage über SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer.

Konfiguration & Fehlerbehandlung

Die Konfiguration der Zeitbasen erfolgt im Manifest (Definition von PTP-Domänen, Sendeintervallen, Grenzwerten für Drift und maximal zulässige Abweichungen). Tritt ein Synchronisationsverlust, ein Telegramm-Timeout oder ein unzulässiger Zeitsprung ein, greifen definierte Fehlerstrategien:

  • Synchronisationsverlust und Timeouts: Bleiben Synchronisationsnachrichten aus oder überschreitet die Drift den Toleranzbereich, wechselt der Zustand von kSynchronized nach kTimeout bzw. kUnsynchronized. Der StatusChangeNotifier alarmiert die Applikation unverzüglich [SWS_TS_01010].
  • Zeitsprünge (Time Leaps): Größere Korrektursprünge (z. B. bei Umschaltung auf eine alternative Master-Quelle oder bei Schaltsekunden) werden über den TimeLeapNotifier signalisiert [SWS_TS_01014], sodass zeitabhängige Algorithmen (z. B. Filter oder Integratoren) ihre internen Zustände konsistent nachführen können.
  • Benutzerdaten-Fallback: Sind in der synchronisierten Zeitbotschaft keine User Data enthalten, signalisiert GetUserData() dies deterministisch gemäss Spezifikation [SWS_TS_00120].
  • Sichere Degradation: Über GetTimeWithStatus() können sicherheitskritische Konsumenten bei jedem Zeitabruf verifizieren, ob der Zeitstempel innerhalb der geforderten Integritäts- und Präzisionsgrenzen liegt, und bei ungültigem Status in einen abgesicherten Ersatzmodus übergehen.

# Richtlinien für KI-generierte Erklärungen

Diese Datei ist Teil des Kuratierungsprozesses: Sie enthält die inhaltlichen
Leitplanken für alle KI-generierten Texte und Diagramme. Die maschinenlesbaren
Parameter dazu stehen in `ai/policy.json`; beide werden von
`ai_workflow.py auftrag` wörtlich in jeden Regenerierungsauftrag eingebettet.
Änderungen an Policy oder Richtlinien ⇒ `version` in `policy.json` erhöhen;
`ai_workflow.py status` zeigt dann, welche Fragmente noch mit einer älteren
Version erzeugt wurden.

## Geltungsbereich und Sprache

- Kanonische Sprache ist Deutsch (`site.json → sprachen.kanonisch`). KI-Inhalte
  werden ausschließlich deutsch erzeugt; die Übersetzung ist ein nachgelagerter
  Schritt (i18n_*.py) und niemals Teil der Generierung.
- API-Bezeichner, Typnamen, Enum-Werte, Code und `[SWS_…]`-Kennungen bleiben
  in jeder Sprache unverändert.

## Strukturelle Invarianten

- Jedes Fragment ist genau ein `<div class="ai …">` (Varianten: `ai` für
  Abschnitte, `ai usage` für Verwendungshinweise an Records, `ai module-guide`
  für Modul-Leitfäden) mit Badge und abschließender `<p class="ai-note">`
  (KI-Hinweis). Bestehende Fragmente sind die Referenz.
- Fragmente liegen unter `content/ai/<seiten-verzeichnis>/` und heißen
  `rec_<ELEMENT-ID>_<NN>.html` (an ein Spezifikationselement gebunden) oder
  `main_<NN>.html` (seitenbezogen).

## Belegpflicht und Quellen

- Jede fachliche Aussage ist mit `[SWS_…]`/`[RS_…]`-Zitat zu belegen
  (`policy.zitierpflicht`); Zitate verlinken auf das Quelldokument (PDF mit
  `#nameddest`), Richtwert `policy.relevanz.min_zitate_je_absatz`.
- Es dürfen nur Dokumente aus dem Quellenregister `ai/quellen.json` verwendet
  werden. Neue Quellen werden zuerst dort registriert (id, titel, typ, url).
- Aus Quellen extrahierte Einzelaussagen, auf die sich ein Text stützt, werden
  in der Trace unter `wissen[]` festgehalten: `{"aussage": …, "quelle": <id>,
  "fundstelle": …}`.

## Annahmen (Wissenslücken)

- Wo die Spezifikation schweigt, darf die KI Lücken mit Annahmen schließen —
  höchstens `policy.annahmen.budget_je_text` pro Text bzw.
  `budget_je_diagramm` pro Diagramm.
- Jede Annahme wird (a) im Text als Interpretation erkennbar formuliert und
  (b) in der Trace unter `annahmen[]` protokolliert:
  `{"annahme": …, "begruendung": …}`.
- Reicht das Budget nicht, wird der Aspekt weggelassen — niemals unmarkiert
  spekuliert.

## Diagramm-Entscheidung

Ein Diagramm wird nur eingefügt, wenn es gegenüber dem Text Mehrwert bietet
(`policy.diagramme`):

- Sequenzdiagramm (`.seq.json`): Abläufe mit ≥ `sequenz_ab_schritten`
  Schritten oder nicht offensichtlicher Reihenfolge/Asynchronität.
- Kontext-/Strukturdiagramm (`.dot`): ≥ `kontext_ab_beteiligten` beteiligte
  Komponenten oder nicht-triviale Vererbungs-/Abhängigkeitscluster.
- Zustandsdiagramm (`.dot`): Lebenszyklen und Zustandsmaschinen.
- Keine Trivialdiagramme (einzelne Aufrufe, Getter/Setter, Zweierbeziehungen).

Die Entscheidung („warum dieses Diagramm, warum diese Form“), etwaige
Annahmen und das Denk-Transkript zur Quellenerstellung gehören in die Trace
unter `diagramme["<quellpfad>"]` — nicht ins HTML. Diagrammquellen liegen als
`<fragment-stem>.<diag-id>.dot|.seq.json` neben dem Fragment (inline) bzw.
unter `diagrams/` (seitenweite Diagramme); gerendert wird mit
`render_diagrams.py`. Beschriftungen deutsch, Bezeichner unverändert.

      "source_page": 7,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n8.5.3.1 SetPdelayInitiatorData . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 79\n8.5.3.2 SetSlaveTimingData . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 79\n8.6 C++ Time Precision Interface . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 80\n8.6.1 Type definitions . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 80\n8.6.1.1 TimePrecisionMeasurement type . . . . . . . . . . . . 80\nA Mentioned Class Tables 83\nB Interfaces to other Functional Clusters (informative) 87\nB.1 Overview . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 87\nB.2 Interface Tables . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 87\nC Change history of AUTOSAR traceable items 88\nC.1 Traceable item history of this document according to AUTOSAR Re-\nlease R23-11 . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 88\nC.1.1 Added Specification Items in R23-11 . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 88\nC.1.2 Changed Specification Items in R23-11 . . . . . . . . . . . . . 88\nC.1.3 Deleted Specification Items in R23-11 . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 88\n7 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P8_08",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 8,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n1 Introduction and functional overview\nTime Synchronization between different applications and/or ECUs is of paramount im-\nportance when correlation of different events across a distributed system is needed,\neither to be able to track such events in time or to trigger them at an accurate point in\ntime.\nFor this reason, a Time Synchronization API is offered to the Application, so it can\nretrieve the time information synchronized with other entities / ECUs.\nFor the format, message sequences and semantics of the time synchronization pro-\ntocols to use, please refer to the Protocol Requirements Specicification (PRS) of the\nAUTOSAR Time synchronization Protocol (see [1]).\nThe Time Synchronization functionality is then offered by means of different \"Time\nBase Resources\" (from now on referred to as TBR).\nThese TBRs are classified in different types. These types have an equivalent design\nto the types of the time bases offered in the Synchronized Time Base Manager speci-\nfication [2] (from now on referred to as StbM). The classification is the following:\n•\nSynchronized Master Time Base\n•\nOffset Master Time Base\n•\nSynchronized Slave Time Base\n•\nOffset Slave Time Base\nAs in StbM, the TBRs offered by the Time Synchronization module (TS from now on),\nare also synchronized with other Time Bases on other nodes of a distributed system.\nThe Application consumes the time information provided and managed by the TBRs.\nTherefore, the TBRs serve as Time Base brokers, offering access to Synchronized\nTime Bases. By doing so, the TS module abstracts from the \"real\" Time Base provider.\n8 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P9_09",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 9,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n2 Acronyms and Abbreviations\nThe glossary below includes acronyms, abbreviations and definitions relevant to the\nTime Synchronization module that are not included in the [3, AUTOSAR glossary] or in\n[4].\n2.1 Acronyms and Abbreviations"
    },

    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P11_13",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 11,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n3 Related documentation\n3.1 Input documents & related standards and norms\n[1] Time Synchronization Protocol Specification\nAUTOSAR_FO_PRS_TimeSyncProtocol\n[2] Specification of Synchronized Time-Base Manager\nAUTOSAR_CP_SWS_SynchronizedTimeBaseManager\n[3] Glossary\nAUTOSAR_FO_TR_Glossary\n[4] Requirements on Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR_FO_RS_TimeSync\n[5] General Requirements specific to Adaptive Platform\nAUTOSAR_AP_RS_General\n[6] Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core\n[7] Explanation of Adaptive Platform Software Architecture\nAUTOSAR_AP_EXP_SWArchitecture\n[8] ISO/IEC 14882:2011, Information technology  Programming languages  C++\nhttps://www.iso.org\n[9] Standard for Information TechnologyPortable Operating System Interface\n(POSIX(R)) Base Specifications, Issue 7\nhttp://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/\n[10] Specification of Time Synchronization over Ethernet\nAUTOSAR_CP_SWS_TimeSyncOverEthernet\n[11] Specification of Manifest\nAUTOSAR_AP_TPS_ManifestSpecification\nNOTE: [5, RS-RSGeneral] is listed here as an input document because it applies to\nSWS TimeSync as well as to all SWS documents of the Adaptive Platform. Since it\nincludes only non-functional requirements the tracing is not necessary.\n3.2 Further applicable specification\nAUTOSAR provides a core specification [6, SWS AdaptiveCore] which is also appli-\ncable for\nTime Synchronization\n. The chapter \"General requirements for all Func-\ntional Clusters\" of this specification shall be considered as an additional and required\nspecification for implementation of\nTime Synchronization\n.\n11 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P12_14",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 12,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4 Constraints and assumptions\n4.1 Known limitations\nThe Time Synchronization module is bound to Adaptive Platform Systems.\n4.1.1 Configuration\nPlease refer to the corresponding model elements.\n4.1.2 Time Gateway\nTime Gateway functionality is currently not in scope of the Time Synchronization mod-\nule for the Adaptive Platform.\n4.1.3 Out of Scope\nErrors, which occurred during Global Time establishment and which are not caused by\nthe module itself (i.e. loss of PTP global time is not an issue of the TS but of the TSP\nmodules) are out of the scope of this module.\n4.1.4 Security\nSecured Time Synchronization using the AUTOSAR Sub-TLV: Time Authenticated (see\nPRS-TimeSync [1]) is currently not supported for the Adaptive Platform.\nNote:\nSecured Time Synchronization messages received in AP ECUs works with-\nout verifying the security measures (i.e., AUTOSAR Sub-TLV:Time Authenticated is\nignored).\n4.1.5 Offset Time Bases\nThe Time Synchronization module of the Adaptive Platform does not support rate cor-\nrection for Offset Time Bases.\n12 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P13_15",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 13,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4.2 Applicability to car domains\nThe concept is targeted at supporting time-critical automotive applications. This does\nnot mean that the concept has all that is required by such systems though, but crucial\ntiming-related features which cannot be deferred to implementation are considered.\n4.3 Recommendation\nIn the case where the TSP is based on Ethernet, the protocol to be used is defined in\nthe PRS (see [1]).\n...\n13 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P14_16",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 14,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n5 Dependencies to other Functional Clusters\nThis chapter provides an overview of the dependencies to other Functional Clusters\nin the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform. Section 5.1 Provided Interfaces lists the inter-\nfaces provided by\nTime Synchronization\nto other Functional Clusters. Section\n5.2 Required Interfaces lists the interfaces required by\nTime Synchronization\n.\nA detailed technical architecture documentation of the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform is\nprovided in [7].\n5.1 Provided Interfaces"
    },

    {

      "source_page": 20,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "4\n[SWS_TS_14161] [SWS_TS_14162]\n[SWS_TS_14163] [SWS_TS_14164]\n[SWS_TS_14165] [SWS_TS_14166]\n[SWS_TS_14167] [SWS_TS_14170]\n[SWS_TS_14171] [SWS_TS_14172]\n[SWS_TS_14173] [SWS_TS_14174]"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P21_53",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 21,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7 Functional specification\nThe functional behavior is described under the following specific contexts:\n•\nStartup Behavior\n•\nShutdown Behavior\n•\nConstruction Behavior (Initialization)\n•\nNormal Operation\n•\nError Handling\n•\nError Classification\n•\nVersion Check\n7.1 General Overview of TS\nFor the Adaptive Platform, three different technologies were considered to fulfill such\nTime Synchronization requirements. These technologies were:\n•\nStbM of the Classic Platform\n•\nLibrary chrono - either std::chrono (C++11) or boost::chrono [8]\n•\nThe Time posix interface [9]\nThe following table shows the interfaces provided to the Application by means of this\nAPI and their equivalent interface in StbM."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P22_54",
      "source_element": "SWS_TS_00202",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 22,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P22_55",
      "source_element": "SWS_TS_00202",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 22,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Table 7.1: Interface comparison between TS and STBM\n7.1.1 Base functionality of every Time Base\nEvery Time Base has to provide a minimum set of functionality, as listed below:\n•\noffer possibility to obtain the current timestamp\n•\ncreating a snapshot of its parameters\nThis chapter briefly describes these functionalities. Details on how to use and the exact\nbehavior of these core methods are given in chapter 8.\n7.1.1.1 Time Base Status\nThis\nTimeBaseStatus\nis a snapshot of all the information of a Time Base Resource\nit is related to, like status flags, amount of times the TBR has been updated, time\nleap information (possibly generated during the last synchronization of the Time Base\nResource), etc.\n7.1.1.2 Rate Deviation\nApplications will have different thresholds for acceptable time drift values. Hence there\nneeds to be a way, how applications can access this information.\n[SWS_TS_00202]\n⌈\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer::Ge-\ntRateDeviation\nshall return the calculated rate deviation of its TBR against the\ntime source it is synchronized to. In case there is no rate deviation calculated yet, the\ninitial rate deviation of 0.0 shall be returned.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00018)\nNote:\nFor more information of how rate deviation is calculated see: 7.3.6 Time Correc-\ntion.\n7.1.1.3 Clock Time Value\nReading the clock's time value is very likely the most commonly performed operation\nby the applications interacting with TS.\n22 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P23_56",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 23,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nTo ensure type safe handling of time values, the timepoint is provided as std::chrono\nstructure.\nMore detailed information on how this is implemented is given in the further chapters\nand in chapter 8.\n7.1.2 Status Flags of TBRs\nTime Synchronization defines a set of status flags that are used to express specific\nstatus conditions of a TBR. Status flags can be queried by an application through a\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer::GetTimeWithStatus\n.\nSynchronization status GetSynchronizationStatus includes:\n•\nkNotSynchronizedUntilStartup\n: Indicates whether a synchronization of a\ntime base to its corresponding TBR happend until start-up (initial state)\n•\nkTimeOut\n: Indicates whether a synchronization of a time base to its correspond-\ning TBR is lost or delayed.\n•\nkSynchronized\n: Indicates if the time base of the corresponding TBR has been\nsuccessfully synchronized at least once against its time source.\n•\nkSynchToGateway\n: Indicates if the corresponding TBR updates are based on\na Time Gateway below the Global Time Master.\nThe status if a leap jump happend since the last status request through a GetTime-\nWithStatus could be retrieved via GetLeapJump:\n•\nkTimeLeapNone\n: Indicates that no leap jump happend\n•\nkTimeLeapFuture\n: Indicates if there has been a jump in time to the future.\n•\nkTimeLeapPast\n: Indicates if there has been a jump in time to the past.\n7.1.3 Time Synchronization and Protocols\nTime Synchronization mechanisms and protocols (i.e. [10] are out of the Scope of this\ndocument, for protocol specification please refer to the PRS (see [1]).\n7.2 Functional cluster life cycle\n7.2.1 Startup\nThis chapter describes the necessary initializations, which are performed by the entity\nthat has control over the Time Base Resources, in order to prepare the TS module for\n23 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P24_57",
      "source_element": "SWS_TS_14175",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 24,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nnormal operation. After its initialization, the module is expected to provide all synchro-\nnized time services to the applications.\n[SWS_TS_14175]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nA TBR configured as Time Master shall start the trans-\nmission of sync message only if the network is available (link is up) and in one of the\nfollowing conditions:\n•\na valid time is set or updated by the application or\n•\nthe backupTimeStamp is successfully restored from persistent memory\n⌋\n(RS_TS_20047, RS_TS_20058)\n[SWS_TS_00213]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nFor each TBR configured as Time Master for\nwhich storage to persistent memory is activated, i.e. a '\nTimeBaseProvider-\nToPersistencyMapping\n.\ntimeBaseProvider\n' is present, the value of\nGlobal Time shall be restored from persistent memory such that the value\nof\nbackupTimestamp\nis used to initialize the Time Base. Immediately\nafter successfully loading the stored\nbackupTimestamp\n, the Time Mas-\nter shall store a\nnew backupTimestamp\n(\n=\nloaded\n(\nold\n)\nbackupT imestamp\n+\nTimeBaseProviderToPersistencyMapping\n:\ncyclicBackupInterval\n)\n⌋\n(RS_-\nTS_00024, RS_TS_00004)\n[SWS_TS_00214]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nIn case the restore from persistent memory is not suc-\ncessful, the Time Base shall start with zero.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00024)\n[SWS_TS_00215]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nFor each TBR configured as Time Slave,\nClock Update\nCounter\nshall be initialized with zero.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00024)\n7.2.1.1 Default values\nWhen the system starts up, the TBRs have to be set to known default values so that\ntheir behavior is well defined.\n[SWS_TS_00007]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nCharacteristics of Time Base Resources shall be initial-\nized as follows:\n•\nActive Status Flags shall be invalidated.\n•\nThe User Data is to be deleted.\n•\nTime Leap information shall be reset.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00009)\n7.2.2 Shutdown\n[SWS_TS_00212]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nFor each TBR configured as Time Master for which stor-\nage to persistent memory is activated, i.e a '\nTimeBaseProviderToPersisten-\n24 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P25_58",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 25,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\ncyMapping\n.\ntimeBaseProvider\n' is present, first the current value of the Global Time\nshall be read every '\nTimeBaseProviderToPersistencyMapping\n.\ncyclicBack-\nupInterval\n'. Then the value of the '\nTimeBaseProviderToPersistencyMap-\nping\n.\ncyclicBackupInterval\n' itself shall be added and this check-pointed value\nof the Global Time shall then be stored into persistent memory '\nTimeBaseProvider-\nToPersistencyMapping\n.\ntimeBaseProvider\n' (see [11]) as\nbackupTimestamp\nif\npersistent storage is required. The initial value of\nbackupTimestamp\nshall be set to\n0\n.\nUpon a graceful shutdown the Global Time shall be stored without applying\nanother '\nTimeBaseProviderToPersistencyMapping\n.\ncyclicBackupInterval\n'\nas back-off.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00024)\nNote:\nRegardless of the exact shutdown event, the last stored value of\nbackupTi-\nmestamp\nwill be restored during the next startup (see 7.2.1).\n7.3 Normal Operation\n7.3.1 Introduction\nA Global Time network consists of a Time Master and at least one Time Slave. For\neach Time Domain, the Time Master is distributing the Global Time Base to the con-\nnected Time Slaves via Time Synchronization messages. The Time Slave corrects the\nreceived Global Time Base taking into account the Time Stamp at the transmitter side\nand the own generated receiver Time Stamp.\nThe local time of a Slave Time Base will be maintained autonomously and updated\nwhenever a new time value is received from its associated Master Time Base.\n25 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P26_59",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 26,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P27_60",
      "source_element": "SWS_TS_00139",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 27,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.3.2.2 Time Slave\nIn the role of a Time Slave, the TBR updates its internally-maintained local time to a\nvalue of a Global Time Base, which is provided by the corresponding TSP module.\n7.3.3 Time Base Resources\n7.3.3.1 Slave Time Bases\n[SWS_TS_00139]\n⌈\nMonitoring of time leaps to the future shall only be enabled,\nif a\ntimeLeapFutureThreshold\nis other than zero and\nara::tsync::Syn-\nchronizationStatus\nunequal to\nkNotSynchronizedUntilStartup\n.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_-\n00009)\n[SWS_TS_00140]\n⌈\nMonitoring of time leaps to the past shall only be enabled, if a\ntimeLeapPastThreshold\nis other than zero and\nara::tsync::Synchroniza-\ntionStatus\nunequal to\nkNotSynchronizedUntilStartup\n.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00009)\n[SWS_TS_00141]\n⌈\nA check for time leaps shall be performed on every successful\nsynchronization with the master clock, but only after the clock has been synchronized\nonce (\nara::tsync::SynchronizationStatus\nunequal to\nkNotSynchronize-\ndUntilStartup\n).\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00009)\n[SWS_TS_00027]\n⌈\nIf the adjustment made by the resynchronization exceeded the\nspecified threshold values, the corresponding\nara::tsync::LeapJump\nstatus shall\nbe set to\nkTimeLeapNone\nif no leap jump occurred.\nkTimeLeapFuture\n: if jump oc-\ncured in time to the future greater than\ntimeLeapFutureThreshold\n.\nkTimeLeap-\nPast\n: if jump occured in time to the past greater than\ntimeLeapPastThreshold\n.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00009)\n[SWS_TS_00064]\n⌈\nThe initial value of\nara::tsync::LeapJump\nshall be\nkTime-\nLeapNone\n.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00009)\n[SWS_TS_00028]\n⌈\nActive Time Leap Status\nara::tsync::LeapJump\nshall be set to\nkTimeLeapNone\n, if a consecutive number\ntimeLeapHealingCounter\nof synchro-\nnizations were all below the Time Leap Future and Past Thresholds.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00009)\n[SWS_TS_00030]\n⌈\nEach instance of\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseCon-\nsumer\nshall independently monitor for a synchronization timeout by measuring the time\nsince that last update and a specified timeout duration in\nsyncLossTimeout\n.\n⌋\n(RS_-\nTS_00009)\n[SWS_TS_00032]\n⌈\nIn case of a monitored timeout (refer [SWS_TS_00030]) the\nara::\ntsync::SynchronizationStatus\nshall be set to\nkTimeOut\n.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00009)\n[SWS_TS_00011]\n⌈\nIf the update of the Time Base is successful and\nSYNC_TO_GATEWAY bit is set, the\nara::tsync::SynchronizationStatus\nshall be set to\nkSynchToGateway\n.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00009)\n27 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P28_61",
      "source_element": "SWS_TS_00033",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 28,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_TS_00033]\n⌈\nIf the update of the Time Base is successful and the\nSYNC_TO_GATEWAY bit is NOT set, the\nara::tsync::SynchronizationSta-\ntus\nshall be set to\nkSynchronized\n.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00009)\n7.3.4 Immediate Time Synchronization\nAll TSP Modules are working independently of the TS regarding the handling of the\nbus-specific Time Synchronization protocol (i.e. autonomous transmission of Timesync\nmessages on the bus).\nTime information is passed from a TSP to the TBR. Implementation details as well as\nthe interaction of such a TSP with the TBR are outside of the scope of this specifica-\ntion(for protocol specification please refer to [1]).\n7.3.5 User Data\nUser Data is part of each Time Base. User Data is set by the Global Time Master of\neach Time Base and distributed as part of the Timesync messages.\nUser Data can be used to characterize the Time Base, e.g., regarding the quality of the\nunderlying clock source or regarding the progress of time.\nUser Data consists of a vector of bytes. Due to the frame format of various Timesync\nmessages it might not be possible to transmit the complete vector on every bus system.\nIt is the responsibility of the system designer to use only those User Data bytes in the\nvector that can be distributed inside the vehicle network.\n7.3.6 Time Correction\nTS provides the ability for Time Slaves to perform Rate and Offset Correction of the\nSynchronized TBR and Rate Correction of an Offset Time Base.\nFor Global Time Masters, the TS provides the ability to perform Rate Correction of their\nTime Base(s).\nTime correction can be configured individually for each Time Base.\n7.3.6.1 Rate Correction for Time Slaves\nRate Correction detects and eliminates rate deviations of local instances of Time Bases\nand of Offset Time Bases. Rate Correction determines the rate deviation in the scope\nof a measurement. This rate deviation is used as correction factor which the TBR\nuses to correct the Time Base's time whenever it is read (e.g. in the scope of\nara::\ntsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer::GetCurrentTime\n).\n28 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P29_62",
      "source_element": "SWS_TS_00041",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 29,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_TS_00041]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nThe TBR shall perform Rate Correction measurements\nto determine its rate deviation if\nara::tsync::SynchronizationStatus\nis set to\nkSynchronized\n.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00002, RS_TS_00018)\n[SWS_TS_00042]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nThe TBR shall perform Rate Correction measurements\ncontinuously. The end of a measurement marks the start of the next measurement.\nThe start and end of measurements is always triggered by (and aligned to) the recep-\ntion of time values for Synchronized.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00002, RS_TS_00007, RS_TS_00018,\nRS_TS_00019)"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P29_63",
      "source_element": "SWS_TS_00041",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 29,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.2: Visualization of two parallel measurements.\n[SWS_TS_00043]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nDuring runtime, the Synchronized TBR shall determine\nthe timespan of a Rate Correction measurement on the basis of clock\nara::core::\nSteadyClock\n.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00018)\n[SWS_TS_00044]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nThe TBR shall perform as many simultaneous Rate\nCorrection measurements as configured by the parameter '\nTimeSyncCorrection\n.\nrateCorrectionsPerMeasurementDuration\n'.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00018)\n[SWS_TS_00045]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nSimultaneous Rate Correction measurements shall be\nstarted with a defined offset (to\nn\n) to yield Rate Corrections evenly distributed over the\nmeasurement duration. The value will be calculated according to the following formula:\nto\nn\n= n\n*\n(rateDeviationMeasurementDuration / rateCorrection-\nPerMeasurementDuration)\n(where 'n' is the zero-based index of the current\nmeasurement)\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00018, RS_TS_00019)\n[SWS_TS_00046]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nAt the start of a Rate Correction measurement, the Syn-\nchronized TBR shall take the time-snapshots\nTGStart\nand\nTVStart\nin the scope of\nTSP.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00018)\n[SWS_TS_00047]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nAt the start of a Rate correction measurement, the Offset\nTBR, shall take the following time-snapshots in the scope of TSP:\n•\nTSStart\n•\nTOStart\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00018)\n29 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P30_64",
      "source_element": "SWS_TS_00048",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 30,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_TS_00048]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nAt the end of the Rate Correction measurement, the Syn-\nchronized TBR shall take the time-snapshots\nTGStop\nand\nTVStop\nin the scope TSP.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00018)\n[SWS_TS_00049]\n{OBSOLETE}\n⌈\nAt the end of the Rate Correction measurement, the\nOffset TBR shall take the following time-snapshots in the scope TSP:\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00018)\n[SWS_TS_00050]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nAt the end of a Rate Correction measurement, the Syn-\nchronized TBR shall calculate the resulting correction rate (r\nrc\n) according to the follow-\ning formula:\nr\nrc\n= (TG\nStop\n- TG\nStart\n) / (TV\nStop\n- TV\nStart\n)\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00018, RS_TS_00019)\nNote:\nTo determine the resulting rate deviation the value 1 has to be subtracted from\nr\nrc\n.\n[SWS_TS_00051]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nThe last r\nrc\nvalue has to be used until a new value is\ncalculated.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00018, RS_TS_00019)\n[SWS_TS_00052]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nOffset TBRs shall not perform yet another rate correction,\nbecause this is done by the underlying Synchronized TBR already.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00018,\nRS_TS_00019)\n[SWS_TS_00053]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nOn invocation of\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTime-\nBaseConsumer::GetRateDeviation\nthe TBR shall return the calculated rate devi-\nation (i.e. r\nrc\n-1).\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00018)\n[SWS_TS_00070]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nIf no rate correction r\nrc\nhas yet been calculated,\nara::\ntsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer::GetRateDeviation\nshall return\n0.0.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00018)\n[SWS_TS_00054]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nIf a valid correction rate (r\nrc\n) has been calculated, the\nSynchronized TBR shall apply a Rate Correction.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00018, RS_TS_00019)\n[SWS_TS_00071]\n{OBSOLETE}\n⌈\nIf a valid correction rate (r\noc\n) has been calculated, the\nOffset TBR shall apply a Rate Correction.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00018, RS_TS_00019)\n7.3.6.2 Offset Correction for Time Consumer\nOffset Correction eliminates time offsets of local instances of Synchronized Time\nBases. This correction takes place whenever the current time is read (e.g. in the scope\nof\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer::GetCurrentTime\n). The\noffset is measured when the local instance of the Time Base is synchronized in the\nscope of TSP.\n[SWS_TS_00055]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nFor Synchronized TBRs, it shall be measured the offset\nbetween its local instance of the Time Base and the Global Time Base whenever the\nTime Base is synchronized in the scope of the function TSP by taking a snapshot of\nthe TLSync and TVSync.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00013)\n30 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P31_65",
      "source_element": "SWS_TS_00056",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 31,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_TS_00056]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nIf the absolute value of the time offset between Global\nTime Base and local instance of the Time Base (abs(TG - TL\nSync\n)) is equal or greater\nthan '\nTimeSyncCorrection\n.\noffsetCorrectionJumpThreshold\n', the TBR shall\ncalculate the corrected time (TL) of its local instance of the Time Base according to the\nfollowing formula:\nTL = TG + (TV - TV\nSync\n)\n*\nr\nrc\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00013, RS_TS_00019)\nNote:\nThis correction will be done whenever the time is read in the scope of e.g. the function\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer::GetCurrentTime\n.\nNote:\nThis correction will be done when the TBR needs to determine the time of the local\ninstance of the Time Base.\n[SWS_TS_00057]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nThe TBR shall correct absolute time offsets between the\nGlobal Time Base and the local instance of the Time Base (abs(TG - TL\nSync\n)), which\nare smaller than the value given by '\nTimeSyncCorrection\n.\noffsetCorrection-\nJumpThreshold\n' by temporarily applying an additional rate (r\noc\n) to r\nrc\n. This rate shall\nbe used for the duration defined by parameter '\nTimeSyncCorrection\n.\noffsetCor-\nrectionAdaptionInterval\n'. r\noc\nis calculated according to the following formula:\nr\noc\n= (TG - TL\nSync\n) / (T\nCorrInt\n) + 1\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00013, RS_TS_00019)\n[SWS_TS_00058]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nIf the absolute time offset between Global Time Base\nand local instance of the Time Base (abs(\nTG\n- TL\nSync\n)) is smaller than '\nTimeSync-\nCorrection\n.\noffsetCorrectionJumpThreshold\n', the TBR shall calculate the\ncorrected time (TL) of its local instance of the Time Base\nwithin\nthe period of '\nTimeSyncCorrection\n.\noffsetCorrectionAdaptionInterval\n' according to the\nfollowing formula:\nTL = TL\nSync\n+ (r\nrc\n*\n(TV - TV\nSync\n)\n*\nr\noc\n)\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00013, RS_TS_00019)\nNote:\nThis correction will be done whenever the time is read in the scope of e.g. the function\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer::GetCurrentTime\n.\nNote:\nThis correction will be done when the TBR needs to determine the time of the local\ninstance of the Time Base.\n[SWS_TS_00059]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nIf the absolute time offset between the Global Time\nBase and the local instance of the Time Base (abs(TG - TL)) is smaller than\nTimeSyncCorrection\n.\noffsetCorrectionJumpThreshold\n, the TBR shall calcu-\nlate the corrected time (TL) of its local instance of the Time Base\nafter\nthe period\nof\nTimeSyncCorrection\n.\noffsetCorrectionAdaptionInterval\nas specified in\n[SWS_TS_00056]\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00013)\n31 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P32_66",
      "source_element": "SWS_TS_00060",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 32,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_TS_00060]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nIf\nTimeSyncCorrection\n.\noffsetCorrection-\nJumpThreshold\nis set to 0, Offset Correction shall be performed by Jump Correction\nonly.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00013)\n7.3.6.3 Rate Correction for Global Time Masters\nRate correction in Global Time Masters can be applied to Synchronized and Offset\nTime Bases Resources.\nRate correction is applied by setting a correction factor which the TBR uses to cor-\nrect the Time Base's time whenever it is transmitted over the network. This happens\nindependent of the rate correction done by the slave.\n[SWS_TS_00061]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nIf '\nTimeSyncCorrection\n.\nallowProviderRateCor-\nrection\n' equals\ntrue\n, an invocation of\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBase-\nProvider::SetRateCorrection\nshall set the rate correction value. Otherwise\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseProvider::SetRateCorrection\nshall\ndo nothing and return the error kLimitsExceeded\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00018)\n[SWS_TS_00062]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nThe TBR shall apply rate correction, if\nallowProvider-\nRateCorrection\nequals TRUE and a valid rate correction value has been set\nby\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseProvider::SetRateCorrection\n.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00018)\n[SWS_TS_00063]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nIf the absolute value of the rate correction parame-\nter\nrateCorrection\n, which is passed to\nSetRateCorrection()\n, is greater\nthan\nMasterRateDeviationMax\n,\nSetRateCorrection()\nshall set the actu-\nally applied rate correction value to either (\nMasterRateDeviationMax\n) or (-\nMasterRateDeviationMax\n)(depending on sign of\nrateCorrection\n).\n⌋\n(RS_TS_-\n00018)\nNote:\nThe actual applied resulting rate will be the passed deviation value + 1. If align-\ning the rate of one Time Base to the rate of another one, it is possible to use\nara::\ntsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseProvider::GetRateDeviation\nand pass the\nvalue as argument to\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseProvider::Se-\ntRateCorrection\n.\n7.3.7 Notifications of Time Base Consumer\nThe Application might request to be notified of dedicated events for a specific TBR.\n7.3.7.1 Status flags notification\nA change in the StatusFlags of the\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseStatus\ncan be notified.\n32 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P33_67",
      "source_element": "SWS_TS_00701",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 33,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_TS_00701]\n⌈\nA registered notifier via\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTime-\nBaseConsumer::RegisterStatusChangeNotifier\nshall be invoked, if one of\nthe following content is changed:\nara::tsync::SynchronizationStatus\n,\nara::\ntsync::LeapJump\nor the\nuser data\n.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00021)\n7.3.7.2 Synchronization status notification\nA change in the StatusFlags of the\nara::tsync::SynchronizationStatus\n(e.g.\nif the timebase is in Timeout) can be notified.\n[SWS_TS_00702]\n⌈\nA registered notifier via\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTime-\nBaseConsumer::RegisterSynchronizationStateChangeNotifier\nshall be\ninvoked, if\nara::tsync::SynchronizationStatus\nis changed.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00009)\n7.3.7.3 LeapJump notification\nA leap jump can be notified.\n[SWS_TS_00703]\n⌈\nA registered notifier via\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTime-\nBaseConsumer::RegisterTimeLeapNotifier\nshall be invoked, if\nara::\ntsync::LeapJump\nis changed.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00034)\n7.3.8 Global Time Precision Measurement Support\nTo verify the precision of each Local Time Base compared to the Global Time Base\na recording mechanism shall be optionally supported for Time Slaves and Time Gate-\nways. In principle, a snapshot is taken of all required data at the point in time, where\na synchronization event takes place. Access is provided to those values by an actively\npushed API function on each successful assembled data block. An Off-Board Tester\ncollects each block and calculates the precision afterwards and maintains a history of\nrecorded blocks and their elements accordingly. How and by which protocol the data\nwill be transferred to the Off-Board Tester will be specified by the Application.\n[SWS_TS_00803]\n⌈\nA registration via\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseCon-\nsumer::RegisterTimePrecisionMeasurementNotifier\nshall only be possible\nfor Synchronized Time Bases and Offset Time Bases, for which\nisSystemWideGlob-\nalTimeMaster\nis set to FALSE.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00034)\n[SWS_TS_00800]\n⌈\nFor Synchronized Time Bases, a registered TimePrecisionMea-\nsurement notifier (via\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer::Reg-\nisterTimePrecisionMeasurementNotifier\n) shall write the block elements\n•\nglbSeconds\n•\nglbNanoSeconds\n33 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P34_68",
      "source_element": "SWS_TS_00801",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 34,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n•\ntimeBaseStatus\n•\nvirtualLocalTimeLow\n•\nrateDeviation\n•\nlocSeconds\n•\nlocNanoSeconds\n•\npathDelay\nto the related measurement recording table after updating the Main Time Tuple (i.e.,\nafter updating the Local Time Base by the Global Time Base). GlbSeconds, Glb-\nNanoSeconds are the elements of the Global Time part of the Received Time Tuple\n(i.e., TGRx); VirtualLocalTimeLow is the nanosecondsLo element of the Virtual Local\nTime part of the Received Time Tuple (i.e., TVRx).\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00034)\n[SWS_TS_00801]\n⌈\nFor Offset Time Bases, a registered TimePrecisionMeasure-\nment notifier (via\nara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer::Regis-\nterTimePrecisionMeasurementNotifier\n) shall only write the block elements\nGlbSeconds, GlbNanoSeconds and TimeBaseStatus to the related measurement\nrecording table.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00034)\n7.3.9 Global Time Validation Measurement Support\nFigure 7.3 outlines the basic concept of the Time Validation feature.\nA Time Slave collects information on the time synchronization process, to predict e.g.\nthe Sync Ingress based on its local instance of Global Time and check whether Master\nand Slave agree upon the current time. The prediction itself will be locally analyzed\nby a separate Adaptive Application to detect any existing impairments. Furthermore,\ninformation on the time synchronization process from Time Masters and Slaves is also\nshared with a Validator Adaptive Application which may run anywhere in the network,\ne.g. on the owner of Global Time.\nThe Validator uses the information on the time synchronization process received from\nthe Time Master and Time Slave Entities via a user defined feedback channel to re-\nconstruct the whole synchronization process and check that a coherent time base is\nestablished among all peers.\nThe Time Validation feature only provides API to the Adaptive Application. The feed-\nback channel and the actual validation performed by the respective Adaptive Applica-\ntion is not standardized in AUTOSAR. It is done in a user defined way on application\nlevel.\n34 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"
    },

      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P35_69",
      "source_element": "SWS_TS_00424",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 35,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_tsync_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_T_P35_70",
      "source_element": "SWS_TS_00424",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization",
      "source_page": 35,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.3: Time Validation mechanism\nFor an optional validation of the Timesync and Pdelay mechanisms, the Time Synchro-\nnization functional cluster provides the following functionality.\n[SWS_TS_00424]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nEverytime a\nFollow_Up\nmessage is received, all pa-\nrameters defined by\nara::tsync::TimeSlaveMeasurementType\nshall be up-\ndated and the function\nara::tsync::ConsumerTimeBaseValidationNotifi-\ncation::SetSlaveTimingData\nshall be invoked.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00034)\n[SWS_TS_00425]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nEverytime a Sync message is transmitted, all pa-\nrameters defined by\nara::tsync::TimeMasterMeasurementType\nshall be up-\ndated and the function\nara::tsync::ProviderTimeBaseValidationNotifi-\ncation::SetMasterTimingData\nshall be invoked.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00034)\n[SWS_TS_00426]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nAfter the current Pdelay measurement is finished,\ni.e., upon reception of the\nPdelay_Resp_Follow_Up\nmessage, all parame-\nters defined by\nara::tsync::PdelayInitiatorMeasurementType\nshall be up-\ndated and the function\nara::tsync::ConsumerTimeBaseValidationNotifi-\ncation::SetPdelayInitiatorData\nshall be invoked.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00034)\n[SWS_TS_00427]\n{DRAFT}\n⌈\nAfter the current\nPdelay\nmeasurement is finished, i.e.,\nupon transmission of the\nPdelay_Resp_Follow_Up\n, all parameters defined by\nara::tsync::PdelayResponderMeasurementType\nshall be updated and the\nfunction\nara::tsync::ProviderTimeBaseValidationNotification::Set-\nPdelayResponderData\nshall be invoked.\n⌋\n(RS_TS_00034)\n35 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"
    },

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nB Interfaces to other Functional Clusters (informative)\nNote:\nThis is chapter is created in the scope of the new SWS document template and\nin the current version is not applicable.\nB.1 Overview\nAUTOSAR decided not to standardize interfaces which are exclusively used between\nFunctional Clusters (on platform-level only), to allow efficient implementations, which\nmight depend e.g. on the used Operating System.\nThis chapter provides informative guidelines how the interaction between Functional\nClusters looks like, by clustering the relevant requirements of this document to describe\nInter-Functional Cluster (IFC) interfaces. In addition, the standardized public interfaces\nwhich are accessible by user space applications (see chapters 8 can also be used for\ninteraction between Functional Clusters.\nThe goal is to provide a clear understanding of Functional Cluster boundaries and in-\nteraction, without specifying syntactical details. This ensures compatibility between\ndocuments specifying different Functional Clusters and supports parallel implementa-\ntion of different Functional Clusters. Details of the interfaces are up to the platform\nprovider. Additional interfaces, parameters and return values can be added.\nB.2 Interface Tables\nNo content.\n87 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"
    },

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Time Synchronization\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nC Change history of AUTOSAR traceable items\nPlease note that the lists in this chapter also include traceable items that have been\nremoved from the specification in a later version. These items do not appear as hyper-\nlinks in the document.\nC.1 Traceable item history of this document according to\nAUTOSAR Release R23-11\nC.1.1 Added Specification Items in R23-11\n[SWS_TS_00901] [SWS_TS_00902] [SWS_TS_00903] [SWS_TS_00904] [SWS_-\nTS_00905] [SWS_TS_00906] [SWS_TS_00907] [SWS_TS_00908] [SWS_TS_00909]\n[SWS_TS_00910] [SWS_TS_01061] [SWS_TS_01062] [SWS_TS_01204] [SWS_-\nTS_01300] [SWS_TS_01301] [SWS_TS_14175]\nC.1.2 Changed Specification Items in R23-11\n[SWS_TS_00042] [SWS_TS_00047] [SWS_TS_00049] [SWS_TS_00052] [SWS_-\nTS_00058] [SWS_TS_00064] [SWS_TS_00070] [SWS_TS_00071] [SWS_TS_00202]\n[SWS_TS_00420] [SWS_TS_00421] [SWS_TS_00422] [SWS_TS_00423] [SWS_-\nTS_00803] [SWS_TS_01001] [SWS_TS_01002] [SWS_TS_01003] [SWS_TS_01004]\n[SWS_TS_01005] [SWS_TS_01006] [SWS_TS_01101] [SWS_TS_01102] [SWS_-\nTS_01103] [SWS_TS_01104] [SWS_TS_01105] [SWS_TS_01106] [SWS_TS_01107]\n[SWS_TS_01110] [SWS_TS_01201] [SWS_TS_01202] [SWS_TS_01203] [SWS_-\nTS_01205] [SWS_TS_01206] [SWS_TS_01207] [SWS_TS_01209]\nC.1.3 Deleted Specification Items in R23-11\nnone\n88 of 88 Document ID 880: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization"

  "bisheriges_fragment": "<div class=\"ai module-guide\">\n<p class=\"ai-note\">Automatisch generierte Beschreibung, inhaltlich abgeleitet aus den referenzierten AUTOSAR-R25-11-Dokumenten (SWS-Spezifikation und begleitende Standarddokumente) — kein offizieller AUTOSAR-Text. Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p>\n\n<h3>Rolle &amp; Verwendungszweck</h3>\n<p>Time Synchronization (<code>ara::tsync</code>) stellt der AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform hochpräzise, netzwerkweit synchronisierte Zeitbasen bereit. In modernen Fahrzeugarchitekturen ist eine konsistente Zeitreferenz über mehrere Steuergeräte hinweg unerlässlich — insbesondere für Sensorfusion, bild- und radargestützte Fahrerassistenzsysteme (ADAS), deterministische Ereignisprotokollierung sowie echtzeitkritische Regelungen <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00001\">[SWS_TS_00001]</a>.</p>\n<p>Das Modul realisiert die Anbindung an standardisierte Zeitsynchronisationsprotokolle wie gPTP (IEEE 802.1AS / IEEE 1588) über Ethernet sowie busspezifische Zeitsynchronisationsmechanismen (z. B. CAN-TSyn). Es unterscheidet funktional zwischen Time Master (Knoten, die als globale Zeitquelle fungieren oder Zeitinformationen weiterverteilen) und Time Slave (Knoten, die externe Zeitbotschaften empfangen, Pfadverzögerungen kompensieren und die lokale Uhr disziplinieren) <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00010\">[SWS_TS_00010]</a>.</p>\n\n<h3>Architektur- und Schnittstellenverträge</h3>\n<p>Die C++-Schnittstellen von <code>ara::tsync</code> orientieren sich eng an den Standards von <code>std::chrono</code> und bieten darüber hinaus spezialisierte Verträge für automobilrelevante Zeitstatusprüfungen:</p>\n<ul>\n  <li><strong>SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer:</strong> Zentraler API-Einstiegspunkt für Anwendungen, die eine synchronisierte Zeitbasis konsumieren <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01001\">[SWS_TS_01001]</a>. Über <code>GetCurrentTime()</code> wird ein synchronisierter Zeitstempel als <code>ara::core::Result&lt;TimePoint&gt;</code> abgerufen <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01007\">[SWS_TS_01007]</a>.</li>\n  <li><strong>Ratenabweichung und Zeitstatus:</strong> Mit <code>GetRateDeviation()</code> lässt sich die aktuelle Frequenz- bzw. Ratenabweichung der Uhr (Drift) ermitteln <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01008\">[SWS_TS_01008]</a>. Die Methode <code>GetTimeWithStatus()</code> liefert den Zeitwert atomar zusammen mit dem aktuellen Gültigkeits- und Synchronisationszustand <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01009\">[SWS_TS_01009]</a>.</li>\n  <li><strong>Ereignis- und Statussignalisierung:</strong> Anwendungen können Callback-Handler für Statuswechsel (<code>RegisterStatusChangeNotifier()</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01010\">[SWS_TS_01010]</a>), Änderungen des Synchronisationszustands (<code>RegisterSynchronizationStateChangeNotifier()</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01012\">[SWS_TS_01012]</a>) sowie Zeitspünge (<code>RegisterTimeLeapNotifier()</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01014\">[SWS_TS_01014]</a>) registrieren. Zur Überwachung der Einhaltung vorgegebener Präzisionskorridore dient <code>RegisterTimePrecisionMeasurementNotifier()</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01018\">[SWS_TS_01018]</a>.</li>\n  <li><strong>Statusobjekt SynchronizedTimeBaseStatus:</strong> Kapselt Metadaten zum Synchronisationszustand, darunter Erstellungszeitpunkt (<code>GetCreationTime()</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01055\">[SWS_TS_01055]</a>), Synchronisationsstatus (<code>GetSynchronizationStatus()</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01053\">[SWS_TS_01053]</a>), erkannte Zeitsprünge (<code>GetLeapJump()</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01054\">[SWS_TS_01054]</a>) sowie anwendungsspezifische Benutzerdaten (<code>GetUserData()</code> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01056\">[SWS_TS_01056]</a>).</li>\n  <li><strong>SynchronizedTimeBaseProvider:</strong> Dient Subsystemen, die selbst als lokale oder externe Zeitquelle agieren, zur Bereitstellung und periodischen Einspeisung der Zeitbasis samt Zeitvalidierungsnotifikationen <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01114\">[SWS_TS_01114]</a>.</li>\n</ul>\n\n<h3>Interaktionsfluss</h3>\n<p>Im laufenden Betrieb synchronisiert der Hintergrunddienst von <code>ara::tsync</code> die lokale Uhr kontinuierlich anhand eingehender Protokollbotschaften (z. B. PTP-Sync- und Follow-Up-Frames). Sobald die Zeitabweichung unter den konfigurierten Schwellwert sinkt, meldet das System den Zustand <code>kSynchronized</code> über registrierte Notifier. Konsumierende Anwendungen können jederzeit hochpräzise Zeitstempel abfragen oder auf Statusänderungen reagieren.</p>\n\n<div class=\"diagram\" id=\"diag-01\"><svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer.</p>\n\n<h3>Konfiguration &amp; Fehlerbehandlung</h3>\n<p>Die Konfiguration der Zeitbasen erfolgt im Manifest (Definition von PTP-Domänen, Sendeintervallen, Grenzwerten für Drift und maximal zulässige Abweichungen). Tritt ein Synchronisationsverlust, ein Telegramm-Timeout oder ein unzulässiger Zeitsprung ein, greifen definierte Fehlerstrategien:</p>\n<ul>\n  <li><strong>Synchronisationsverlust und Timeouts:</strong> Bleiben Synchronisationsnachrichten aus oder überschreitet die Drift den Toleranzbereich, wechselt der Zustand von <code>kSynchronized</code> nach <code>kTimeout</code> bzw. <code>kUnsynchronized</code>. Der <code>StatusChangeNotifier</code> alarmiert die Applikation unverzüglich <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01010\">[SWS_TS_01010]</a>.</li>\n  <li><strong>Zeitsprünge (Time Leaps):</strong> Größere Korrektursprünge (z. B. bei Umschaltung auf eine alternative Master-Quelle oder bei Schaltsekunden) werden über den <code>TimeLeapNotifier</code> signalisiert <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_01014\">[SWS_TS_01014]</a>, sodass zeitabhängige Algorithmen (z. B. Filter oder Integratoren) ihre internen Zustände konsistent nachführen können.</li>\n  <li><strong>Benutzerdaten-Fallback:</strong> Sind in der synchronisierten Zeitbotschaft keine User Data enthalten, signalisiert <code>GetUserData()</code> dies deterministisch gemäss Spezifikation <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00120\">[SWS_TS_00120]</a>.</li>\n  <li><strong>Sichere Degradation:</strong> Über <code>GetTimeWithStatus()</code> können sicherheitskritische Konsumenten bei jedem Zeitabruf verifizieren, ob der Zeitstempel innerhalb der geforderten Integritäts- und Präzisionsgrenzen liegt, und bei ungültigem Status in einen abgesicherten Ersatzmodus übergehen.</li>\n</ul>\n</div>\n",

Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p><h4>Globale Zeit als Dienst für Anwendungen</h4><p><code>ara::tsync</code> vermittelt zwischen einer konfigurierten Time Base Resource und Anwendungscode. </div><p class="diagram-note">Einordnung der Provider-/Consumer-API in die Master–Slave-Verteilung. Quelle: <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=section.7.2">SWS Time Synchronization §7.2 „Normal Operation“</a>. <em>Teilweise Interpretation: Die Protokollstrecke abstrahiert die in §7.1.3 aus dem SWS ausgeklammerte PRS-Protokollspezifikation.</em></p><h4>Korrektur und Vertrauenszustand getrennt behandeln</h4><p>Ratekorrektur behandelt Taktabweichungen, Offsetkorrektur behandelt Zeitversatz beim Lesen. Status, Timeout und Leap-Informationen zeigen, ob ein Zeitwert für den jeweiligen Anwendungszweck belastbar ist. {sws(TS,"SWS_TS_00054")} {sws(TS,"SWS_TS_00056")} {sws(TS,"SWS_TS_00032")}</p><h4>Protokoll und API-Grenze</h4><p>Das SWS beschreibt die API und den Master-/Slave-Ablauf, grenzt die Time-Synchronization-Mechanismen und Protokolle jedoch explizit aus und verweist dafür auf die PRS. <em>(Interpretation: Die Modulansicht zeigt deshalb die Protokollstrecke nur als Kontext, nicht als vollständige Wire-Spezifikation.)</em> {T71}</p><h5>Verbindliche §11.2.2.2.1.1 „Get Value Of Time Base"</a>.</p><h4>Verhalten im Fehlerfall</h4>
<p><code>SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer::GetTimeWithStatus()</code> liefert eine Momentaufnahme aus globaler und lokaler Zeit, Synchronisationsstatus, Leap-Status und Nutzdaten. <code>kNotSynchronizedUntilStartup</code> kennzeichnet den Initialzustand, <code>kTimeOut</code> eine verlorene oder verzögerte Synchronisation; erfolgreiche Updates setzen <code>kSynchronized</code> beziehungsweise <code>kSynchToGateway</code>. Jede Consumer-Instanz überwacht den Zeitraum seit dem letzten Update gegen <code>syncLossTimeout</code> und setzt bei Ablauf <code>kTimeOut</code>. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.2">SWS Time Synchronization §7.1.2 „Status Flags of TBRs“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_14218">[SWS_TS_14218]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00030">[SWS_TS_00030]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00032">[SWS_TS_00032]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00011">[SWS_TS_00011]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00033">[SWS_TS_00033]</a></p>
<p>Die Leap-Überwachung ist erst nach einer ersten Synchronisation und nur bei einem von null verschiedenen Schwellwert aktiv. Überschreitet die Resynchronisationsanpassung den jeweiligen Schwellwert, wird <code>LeapJump</code> auf <code>kTimeLeapFuture</code> oder <code>kTimeLeapPast</code> gesetzt; Änderungen des Synchronisations- und Leap-Status können über die vorgesehenen Notifier beobachtet werden. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.7.2.3.1">SWS Time Synchronization §7.2.3.1 „Slave Time Bases“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00139">[SWS_TS_00139]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00140">[SWS_TS_00140]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00141">[SWS_TS_00141]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00027">[SWS_TS_00027]</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.7.2.7.2">SWS Time Synchronization §7.2.7.2 „Synchronization status notification“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00702">[SWS_TS_00702]</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.7.2.7.3">SWS Time Synchronization §7.2.7.3 „LeapJump notification“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00703">[SWS_TS_00703]</a></p>

<p class="diagram-note">Das Zustandsdiagramm zeigt die spezifizierten Synchronisationswerte sowie die getrennt gemeldete Leap-Information. Quellen: <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.7.2.3.1">SWS Time Synchronization §7.2.3.1 „Slave Time Bases“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00030">[SWS_TS_00030]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00032">[SWS_TS_00032]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00027">[SWS_TS_00027]</a>.</p>
<p>Für API-Fehler definiert <code>TsyncErrc</code> die Werte <code>kDaemonConnectionLost</code>, <code>kLimitsExceeded</code>, <code>kFunctionNotSupported</code> und <code>kInvalidUserDataSize</code>. Ein Daemon-Absturz wird bei Setter-APIs hauptsächlich als <code>kDaemonConnectionLost</code>, bei zeitbezogenen Updates wie Nachrichtenverlust mit <code>kTimeOut</code> behandelt. Konkret kann <code>SetTime()</code> bei zu großen Nutzdaten oder verlorener Daemon-Verbindung fehlschlagen; <code>SetRateCorrection()</code> spezifiziert Bereichs- und Unterstützungsfehler. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.8.10.1.1">SWS Time Synchronization §8.10.1.1 „Enumeration: TsyncErrc“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.3.3">SWS Time Synchronization §7.3.3 „Daemon crash“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=subparagraph.8.5.1.1.3.6">SWS Time Synchronization §8.5.1.1.3.6 „SetTime“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=subparagraph.8.5.1.1.3.5">SWS Time Synchronization §8.5.1.1.3.5 „SetRateCorrection“</a></p>

Quelle: <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=section.7.2">SWS Time Synchronization §7.2 „Normal Operation“</a>. <em>Teilweise Interpretation: Die Protokollstrecke abstrahiert die in §7.1.3 aus dem SWS ausgeklammerte PRS-Protokollspezifikation.</em></p><h4>Korrektur und Vertrauenszustand getrennt behandeln</h4><p>Ratekorrektur behandelt Taktabweichungen, Offsetkorrektur behandelt Zeitversatz beim Lesen. Status, Timeout und Leap-Informationen zeigen, ob ein Zeitwert für den jeweiligen Anwendungszweck belastbar ist. {sws(TS,"SWS_TS_00054")} {sws(TS,"SWS_TS_00056")} {sws(TS,"SWS_TS_00032")}</p><h4>Protokoll und API-Grenze</h4><p>Das SWS beschreibt die API und den Master-/Slave-Ablauf, grenzt die Time-Synchronization-Mechanismen und Protokolle jedoch explizit aus und verweist dafür auf die PRS. <em>(Interpretation: Die Modulansicht zeigt deshalb die Protokollstrecke nur als Kontext, nicht als vollständige Wire-Spezifikation.)</em> {T71}</p><h5>Verbindliche §11.2.2.2.1.1 „Get Value Of Time Base"</a>.</p><h4>Verhalten im Fehlerfall</h4> <p><code>SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer::GetTimeWithStatus()</code> liefert eine Momentaufnahme aus globaler und lokaler Zeit, Synchronisationsstatus, Leap-Status und Nutzdaten. <code>kNotSynchronizedUntilStartup</code> kennzeichnet den Initialzustand, <code>kTimeOut</code> eine verlorene oder verzögerte Synchronisation; erfolgreiche Updates setzen <code>kSynchronized</code> beziehungsweise <code>kSynchToGateway</code>. Jede Consumer-Instanz überwacht den Zeitraum seit dem letzten Update gegen <code>syncLossTimeout</code> und setzt bei Ablauf <code>kTimeOut</code>. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.2">SWS Time Synchronization §7.1.2 „Status Flags of TBRs“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_14218">[SWS_TS_14218]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00030">[SWS_TS_00030]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00032">[SWS_TS_00032]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00011">[SWS_TS_00011]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00033">[SWS_TS_00033]</a></p> <p>Die Leap-Überwachung ist erst nach einer ersten Synchronisation und nur bei einem von null verschiedenen Schwellwert aktiv. Überschreitet die Resynchronisationsanpassung den jeweiligen Schwellwert, wird <code>LeapJump</code> auf <code>kTimeLeapFuture</code> oder <code>kTimeLeapPast</code> gesetzt; Änderungen des Synchronisations- und Leap-Status können über die vorgesehenen Notifier beobachtet werden. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.7.2.3.1">SWS Time Synchronization §7.2.3.1 „Slave Time Bases“</a> <a Synchronisationswerte sowie die getrennt gemeldete Leap-Information. Quellen: <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.7.2.3.1">SWS Time Synchronization §7.2.3.1 „Slave Time Bases“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00030">[SWS_TS_00030]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00032">[SWS_TS_00032]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=SWS_TS_00027">[SWS_TS_00027]</a>.</p> <p>Für API-Fehler definiert <code>TsyncErrc</code> die Werte <code>kDaemonConnectionLost</code>, <code>kLimitsExceeded</code>, <code>kFunctionNotSupported</code> und <code>kInvalidUserDataSize</code>. Ein Daemon-Absturz wird bei Setter-APIs hauptsächlich als <code>kDaemonConnectionLost</code>, bei zeitbezogenen Updates wie Nachrichtenverlust mit <code>kTimeOut</code> behandelt. Konkret kann <code>SetTime()</code> bei zu großen Nutzdaten oder verlorener Daemon-Verbindung fehlschlagen; <code>SetRateCorrection()</code> spezifiziert Bereichs- und Unterstützungsfehler. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.8.10.1.1">SWS Time Synchronization §8.10.1.1 „Enumeration: TsyncErrc“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.3.3">SWS Time Synchronization §7.3.3 „Daemon crash“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=subparagraph.8.5.1.1.3.6">SWS Time Synchronization §8.5.1.1.3.6 „SetTime“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_TimeSynchronization.pdf#nameddest=subparagraph.8.5.1.1.3.5">SWS Time Synchronization §8.5.1.1.3.5 „SetRateCorrection“</a></p> </div>

Specification of Time Synchronization
AUTOSAR AP R23-11
1 Introduction and functional overview
Time Synchronization between different applications and/or ECUs is of paramount im-
portance when correlation of different events across a distributed system is needed,
either to be able to track such events in time or to trigger them at an accurate point in
time.
For this reason, a Time Synchronization API is offered to the Application, so it can
retrieve the time information synchronized with other entities / ECUs.
For the format, message sequences and semantics of the time synchronization pro-
tocols to use, please refer to the Protocol Requirements Specicification (PRS) of the
AUTOSAR Time synchronization Protocol (see [1]).
The Time Synchronization functionality is then offered by means of different "Time
Base Resources" (from now on referred to as TBR).
These TBRs are classified in different types. These types have an equivalent design
to the types of the time bases offered in the Synchronized Time Base Manager speci-
fication [2] (from now on referred to as StbM). The classification is the following:
•
Synchronized Master Time Base
•
Offset Master Time Base
•
Synchronized Slave Time Base
•
Offset Slave Time Base
As in StbM, the TBRs offered by the Time Synchronization module (TS from now on),
are also synchronized with other Time Bases on other nodes of a distributed system.
The Application consumes the time information provided and managed by the TBRs.
Therefore, the TBRs serve as Time Base brokers, offering access to Synchronized
Time Bases. By doing so, the TS module abstracts from the "real" Time Base provider.

4 Constraints and assumptions
4.1 Known limitations
The Time Synchronization module is bound to Adaptive Platform Systems.
4.1.1 Configuration
Please refer to the corresponding model elements.
4.1.2 Time Gateway
Time Gateway functionality is currently not in scope of the Time Synchronization mod-
ule for the Adaptive Platform.
4.1.3 Out of Scope
Errors, which occurred during Global Time establishment and which are not caused by
the module itself (i.e. loss of PTP global time is not an issue of the TS but of the TSP
modules) are out of the scope of this module.
4.1.4 Security
Secured Time Synchronization using the AUTOSAR Sub-TLV: Time Authenticated (see
PRS-TimeSync [1]) is currently not supported for the Adaptive Platform.
Note:
Secured Time Synchronization messages received in AP ECUs works with-
out verifying the security measures (i.e., AUTOSAR Sub-TLV:Time Authenticated is
ignored).
4.1.5 Offset Time Bases
The Time Synchronization module of the Adaptive Platform does not support rate cor-
rection for Offset Time Bases.

7 Functional specification
The functional behavior is described under the following specific contexts:
•
Startup Behavior
•
Shutdown Behavior
•
Construction Behavior (Initialization)
•
Normal Operation
•
Error Handling
•
Error Classification
•
Version Check
7.1 General Overview of TS
For the Adaptive Platform, three different technologies were considered to fulfill such
Time Synchronization requirements. These technologies were:
•
StbM of the Classic Platform
•
Library chrono - either std::chrono (C++11) or boost::chrono [8]
•
The Time posix interface [9]
The following table shows the interfaces provided to the Application by means of this
API and their equivalent interface in StbM.

7.1.1 Base functionality of every Time Base
Every Time Base has to provide a minimum set of functionality, as listed below:
•
offer possibility to obtain the current timestamp
•
creating a snapshot of its parameters
This chapter briefly describes these functionalities. Details on how to use and the exact
behavior of these core methods are given in chapter 8.
7.1.1.1 Time Base Status
This
TimeBaseStatus
is a snapshot of all the information of a Time Base Resource
it is related to, like status flags, amount of times the TBR has been updated, time
leap information (possibly generated during the last synchronization of the Time Base
Resource), etc.
7.1.1.2 Rate Deviation
Applications will have different thresholds for acceptable time drift values. Hence there
needs to be a way, how applications can access this information.
[SWS_TS_00202]
⌈
ara::tsync::SynchronizedTimeBaseConsumer::Ge-
tRateDeviation
shall return the calculated rate deviation of its TBR against the
time source it is synchronized to. In case there is no rate deviation calculated yet, the
initial rate deviation of 0.0 shall be returned.
⌋
(RS_TS_00018)
Note:
For more information of how rate deviation is calculated see: 7.3.6 Time Correc-
tion.
7.1.1.3 Clock Time Value
Reading the clock's time value is very likely the most commonly performed operation
by the applications interacting with TS.
